prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect, and for its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I move my first choice from inflation (B032) to the topological-insulator entry (B038). My opening placed B038 third, and the debate has made me weigh two things more heavily. First, B038 is the one entry that most of the committee ranked highly (four top-three placements, six of eight members ranking it), so I am no longer confident my own high ranking of inflation reflects a view that can be defended on the merits against the others. Second, B038 fits what I think the committee's task is, namely identifying a discovery and then the people behind it. The Kane-Mele Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall prediction (2005) were followed within two years by Molenkamp's observation of helical edge conduction in HgTe (2007), so this is a prediction that nature confirmed, later extended by ARPES to three-dimensional materials. The concept changed how band structures are classified and searched for in materials. A three-person theory-plus-experiment prize is natural, and the supplied credit set maps onto it directly.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The HgTe realisation was proposed by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who are not among the credited names, and the three-dimensional topological insulator work (Fu-Kane-Mele, Moore-Balents, Hsieh-Hasan) lies outside this entry. A prize to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp could be read as leaving out the person who identified the platform in which the effect was seen. There is also a conceptual-overlap worry with the 2016 prize on topological phases and phase transitions, and the practical payoff (dissipationless edge transport, spintronics) has not materialised. If those concerns weigh heavily, the committee might prefer a discovery with a cleaner attribution chain.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks B038 first because the Z2 classification reshaped condensed-matter physics, has fifteen years of independent confirmation in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and Bi2Se3, and is arguably overdue after the 2016 prize.
responses.response: I agree on the scientific merit and the maturity. Where I want to qualify is the idea that the credit chain is settled. You describe the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal as a background wrinkle, but without it Molenkamp's HgTe experiment would not have been designed as it was. I would not call the three-name configuration clean. I accept it only because Molenkamp's observation and the Kane-Mele theory are each decisive on their own, and I think the citation should be worded around the prediction of the effect and the first observation so that it does not claim the HgTe proposal as part of the laureates' contribution.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks (B046) first as the clearest case in which a laser-spectroscopy technique changed what can be measured, with several independent laboratories reaching the 1e-18 level and a redefinition of the second under way.
responses.response: I respect the case and I list B046 among the serious candidates, but I disagree that it should lead. The achievement is a very fine instrument and a refinement of precision timekeeping that the committee has already recognised in 2005 (frequency combs) and 2012 (single-ion control). The physics is a better way of making one measurement rather than a new observation about nature, which is the distinction I draw between a discovery and an engineering advance. I would also not wait for the redefinition of the second, since it would add nothing scientifically. If the committee is intent on a metrology prize I would not oppose it, but I do not think it should be ahead of a result that changed our understanding of electronic phases.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B046 first and B017 (quantum key distribution) second, and she places B038 third, noting that credit for HgTe theory is only partial and that the 2016 prize overlaps conceptually.
responses.response: I share your doubt about the incomplete credit, and I think it is the real obstacle for B038. On the 2016 overlap I disagree: the 2016 prize was about topological phase transitions and Hall conductance in the integer quantum Hall setting, with topology a property of the many-body state, while Kane-Mele is time-reversal-invariant and driven by spin-orbit coupling with no magnetic field, a distinct set of concepts. On QKD I agree it is a lovely idea, but I put it seventh in my opening because its prize-worthiness rests on a protocol rather than on an observation, and its practical security is still contested.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks twisted bilayer graphene (B042) first because Bistritzer-MacDonald predicted the magic-angle flat bands before the 2018 discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity.
responses.response: A prediction followed by an experimental discovery is exactly what I look for, so I take the case seriously, and I ranked it sixth rather than lower. My concern is maturity. The pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene is still disputed and the phase diagram is sample dependent, and as a theorist I am wary of recognising a field before we know what the superconductivity is. The topological-insulator case has had a longer period of independent confirmation. I would see B042 as a strong candidate in a few years rather than in 2026, but I accept that you may judge the discovery itself to be secure enough.

uncertainties: Whether the credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) can be set aside without making the prize unfair, given the three-person limit and the credited names.
Whether the committee regards the optical lattice clock (B046) as a discovery or as an advance of technique, since its support is concentrated in three first-place votes.

My own ranking of inflation (B032) depends on how much weight the committee gives to a theory that fits the CMB but has no primordial gravitational-wave detection and unresolved priority questions around Starobinsky; I am recalling that history from memory.
Whether Halzen alone (B025) can be a fair attribution for IceCube, since the supplied credit names a single person and the collaboration is large.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B038. I do work in theoretical high-energy physics and cosmology, which makes me closer to B032 (inflation) and I hold no known connection to its candidates. My documented connections (David Gross, Hector Rubinstein, Thomas Van Riet and the Uppsala theory group) do not involve any shortlisted candidate.
